## (1) First message to the user

I could check one claim directly, and it contradicts a ticket row. Ticket row 2, "The export includes the owner column," assumes the table has an owner column. `src/export/csv.ts:40` shows the table columns are only `["title", "status"]`. The gather draft also records that the exporter reuses the table's column definitions, so there is no owner column to export. The design continues on that corrected fact. Reply if you want to override it.

Two other premises are unverified:

- **No export action today.** The gather draft says the reports page has no export action. I could not confirm this from primary code because the only source available to me is `src/export/csv.ts`. The design treats it as an assumption.
- **The 10k-row timing row.** "The export of a 10k-row report completes in under 60s" depends on a 10k-row report dataset and a way to time the export. No fixture, script, or repo instruction names either one. This goes to Open Questions.

The ticket has no repo groups, and the overrides set `repo: acme/widgets`. All three rows therefore belong to this repo.

The framing holds. I checked `src/export/csv.ts:40`: the exporter draws its columns from the table's own list, so adding an export uses the existing table contract rather than creating a second one. I also checked the reports-page claim, which I could not verify from the files I have, and the timing row's missing dataset and harness. None of these points to a better-sized alternative to "add an export button."

Where should the Export CSV button appear?
A) Beside the report title
B) In a toolbar above the table
C) In a row-actions or overflow menu
other - name it
Recommendation: A - the title area applies to the whole report, and a CSV export covers the whole report, not a row.

---

## (2) Approaches message

**Not sent yet.** You answered D to the owner-column question. The repair was then cancelled at the shape-ticket gate, and the ticket row is unchanged. That returns us to the cut question, which has no recorded answer. Approaches depend on how this row is handled, so the next message re-asks it in full with the row unchanged:

> Ticket row "The export includes the owner column." conflicts with `src/export/csv.ts:40`, where the table columns are only `title` and `status`. The ticket repair was cancelled, so the row still reads as written. How should the spec treat it?
> A) in-scope - add `owner` to the shared column list at `src/export/csv.ts:40`, so the export and the on-page table both show it
> B) deviates: omit the owner column from the export
> C) deferred: acme/widgets#78
> D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77, because src/export/csv.ts:40 has no owner column
> Recommendation: A - the row can ship in this gauntlet through the single column source the exporter already reads. The cost is that the on-page table gains the column too, and the source of owner data is still unverified.

Once you answer, the approaches message will read as follows. The owner-column details assume answer A.

Before the approaches, here are the dependencies I could not check. The 10k-row timing row needs a 10k-row report dataset and a way to time an export. I looked through the available fixture files and found neither, and no repo instruction names one. The gather draft's claim that the reports page has no export action is also unverified, because the reports page source is not available to me. Both stay in Open Questions.

The two approaches differ on one point: whether the existing exporter's single-pass build is assumed fast enough for 10k rows.

**Recommended: wire the button to the existing exporter.** This is the reuse-only option. A new Export CSV button beside the report title calls the existing `src/export/csv.ts` exporter. That exporter already takes its columns from the table's list, so the table and the export cannot drift apart. Under answer A, `owner` is added to `tableColumns` at line 40, and the table and export gain the column together. The blast radius is that every other reader of `tableColumns` also gets the column. The trade-off is that 10k-row performance is whatever the current exporter delivers, which nobody has measured.
Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button beside the report title on the reports page; click handler calling the `src/export/csv.ts` exporter; under A, `"owner"` in `tableColumns` at `src/export/csv.ts:40`; tests for button presence, exported header columns, and a 10k-row timing check
Pattern: follows the single column source at `src/export/csv.ts:40`; no second column list.

**Alternative: add a streaming mode to the same exporter.** This option drops the assumption that a single in-memory build fits within 60s. It adds a chunked or streamed write as a parameter on the existing `src/export/csv.ts` exporter, still reading `tableColumns`. The button and the owner handling are the same as above. This is still a change to the shared exporter, but it adds a code path, and it pays off only if the timing check fails.
Removes: none
Adds: streaming/chunked parameter on the `src/export/csv.ts` exporter; the same button, handler, and owner change as above; the same tests plus a test of streamed output
Pattern: extends the existing exporter in place, as a parameter rather than a parallel exporter, keeping `src/export/csv.ts:40` the sole column source.

I considered an export-only column list that carries `owner` without touching the table. It is not an approach: it would add a second column source beside `src/export/csv.ts:40`, which is the parallel state this design avoids.

What would flip the recommendation: if a 10k-row timing run of the existing exporter exceeds 60s, choose the streaming mode.

### 1. First message to the user

The supplied fixture confirms that `src/export/csv.ts:40` defines only `title` and `status`; it does not establish that adding an owner column is impossible. The draft reports reuse of the table’s column definitions, but the fixture does not show the consumers or data paths needed to verify that claim. The 10k-row, under-60-second requirement also remains unverified. I’ll retain your decision to place the button beside the report title.

The ticket repair was cancelled, so this acceptance row remains unchanged:

> The export includes the owner column.

How should we handle that row?
A) in-scope - add owner to the export, resolving its source and the shared table-column contract in the design.
B) deviates: omit owner from the export.
C) deferred: acme/widgets#78.
D) repair the ticket - /skill:shape-ticket acme/widgets#77, addressing the owner-column row and the evidence that `src/export/csv.ts:40` currently lists only title and status.
Recommendation: A - the existing column list shows a gap to implement, not proof that the ticket requirement cannot ship.

### 2. Approaches message

Pending your answer to the re-opened scope question. Cancelling ticket repair does not authorize omitting or deferring the owner requirement, so I would not advance to approaches yet.
